Subject: Pilot ask — additional credits + 2-week extension?

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday — very helpful. We kicked off some internal tests against the sandbox you provided and we bumped into token limits quickly. The initial plan for our accelerator cohort assumes heavier generation (interactive assistants + batch indexing) so the credit pool will not stretch to the first milestone.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a one-time top-up of 200k tokens for the pilot (one month)?
- Also, would you consider a 2-week trial extension so we can complete the milestoned demo for our investors?

I attached a short one-page proposal with expected token profile and milestones (foundry_proposal_v2.pdf).

We’re targeting a signed pilot SOW by mid-December if this looks feasible. Happy to hop on a quick sync.

Hi Elena — thanks for the proposal and for the clear usage estimates. Short answer: we can usually support a one-time top-up and short extension for accelerator partners, but larger increments require an approval path.

To move quickly I need a couple of things from you:
1) a two-line breakdown of how the 200k tokens will be consumed across interactive vs. batch flows (approx %),
2) the preferred milestone date that the extension would cover (e.g., final demo week), and
3) confirmation that FoundryCV will sign the standard pilot SOW (I’ve attached the SOW template).

Operational notes:
- Top-ups over 150k tokens follow our credit governance review.
- If approved, top-up will be applied to your sandbox project and will be non-refundable; we can instrument cost alerts and per-route caps so you don’t exceed expected spend.

I’m looping in Ben (sales lead) and Priyom (programs) to expedite the review. Ben/Priyom — flag if we need leadership sign-off or if a discount/commitment should be discussed as part of this increment.

Elena — can you shoot the short breakdown today so we can start the governance review? I can clear the extension in parallel if the usage justifies it.

Cheers,
Ava Chen
Senior Growth Manager, Startups
Redwood Inference
